sections.markdown:
## C — Brake lights, mirrors, brakes and ABS, tires, horn, exhaust, suspension, flashers, fuel-saving habits, scanning, signaling, hand signals and safety margins (North Carolina)
Knowledge domain: the equipment a North Carolina vehicle must carry and keep working (stop and turn lights, mirrors, brakes, tires, horn, muffler and exhaust, suspension, hazard flashers), fuel-saving habits, and the defensive driving skills of scanning, communicating, hand signals, keeping a safety margin and adjusting to danger.

FACT_ID: sec11-F01 | anchor: A01
Every motor vehicle built since 1955 must have red or amber lights that come on with the brakes or turn signals, visible for at least 100 feet in normal daylight. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec11-F02 | anchor: A01
Those brake and turn lights may be built into the taillights or mounted separately; either arrangement is allowed. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec11-F03 | anchor: A01
Keep light lenses clean and the lights working, because hand signals are hard for other drivers to see after dark. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec11-F04 | anchor: A01
Check and set the mirrors before driving: the inside mirror shows straight behind, and the side mirrors show the left and right rear while just barely showing the car's own side. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec11-F05 | anchor: A01
Any motor vehicle on a public road must have brakes able to control it, stop it and hold it in place. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec11-F06 | anchor: A01
Factory brakes should be kept in good condition and provide two separate ways of applying the brakes. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec11-F07 | anchor: A01
When pressed all the way, the brake pedal should stay at least one-third of its original distance above the floor; if not, have the brakes checked and repaired. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec11-F08 | anchor: A01
A brake pedal that slowly sinks under steady foot pressure means the hydraulic system needs checking, and squeaking brakes should also be inspected. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec11-F09 | anchor: A01
Anti-lock brakes (ABS) help with stability against spin-outs, with steering where you intend, and with stopping distance. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec11-F10 | anchor: A01
With ABS, brake hard and hold firm, steady pressure; pumping the pedal or easing off reduces how well ABS works. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec11-F11 | anchor: A01
To discourage theft, never leave the key in the ignition of a vehicle you are not attending. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec11-F12 | anchor: A01
A tire is legally unsafe if a cut, crack or wear exposes the cord, if it shows tread separation or chunking, or if tread depth is under 1/16 inch. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec11-F13 | anchor: A01
Under-inflated tires wear out faster and are more likely to blow out, while over-inflated tires lose traction and wear down the center of the tread. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec11-F14 | anchor: A02
Check tire air pressure at least once a month, preferably while the tires are cool, following the manufacturer's recommended pressure. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec11-F15 | anchor: A02
Only law enforcement and emergency vehicles are permitted to carry emergency lights or sirens. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec11-F16 | anchor: A02
Every licensed motor vehicle needs a working horn that can be heard from at least 200 feet without an unreasonably loud or harsh sound. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec11-F17 | anchor: A02
Use the horn only as a reasonable warning, never needlessly, and get a failed horn fixed right away. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec11-F18 | anchor: A02
Every motor vehicle must have a working muffler, which reduces smoke and excess noise. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec11-F19 | anchor: A02
An exhaust leak can let carbon monoxide into the cabin, which can cause drowsiness, unconsciousness or death, so the handbook suggests driving with a window open about one inch. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec11-F20 | anchor: A02
Swaying, leaning hard in turns or constant bouncing can signal a suspension problem, which should be inspected and fixed at once because it can cause loss of control. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec11-F21 | anchor: A02
The emergency flashers blink all four turn signals and may be used by any vehicle to warn of danger or show it is stopped or disabled. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec11-F22 | anchor: A02
For fuel economy, each 5 mph driven above 60 mph can add up to about 30 cents per gallon in cost. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec11-F23 | anchor: A03
Sudden starts and hard stops can raise fuel use by as much as 40 percent. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec11-F24 | anchor: A03
To save fuel, switch off the engine if you will wait more than a couple of minutes, and open the windows below 40 mph but use air conditioning above it. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec11-F25 | anchor: A03
A clogged air filter can lower mileage by about 10 percent, and a loose fuel cap can let up to 30 gallons of gas a year escape. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec11-F26 | anchor: A03
Good drivers look 10 to 15 seconds ahead, roughly one city block, to avoid last-second stops and lane changes. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec11-F27 | anchor: A03
Glance at the mirrors about every 10 seconds to spot a vehicle following too closely, taking your eyes off the road only for an instant. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec11-F28 | anchor: A03
Check behind you and your blind spots when changing lanes, backing, slowing down or going down a long hill. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec11-F29 | anchor: A03
Blind spots are the areas near the left and right rear corners that mirrors cannot show, so turn your head and look over your shoulder before a lane change or turn. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec11-F30 | anchor: A03
Glare, a dirty windshield, cars parked near an intersection, bushes or buildings can also block your view; ease forward until you can see clearly. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec11-F31 | anchor: A03
Signal whenever you plan to slow, stop, turn, change lanes or leave the curb, even with no one in sight, but first confirm the move is safe. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec11-F32 | anchor: A04
Turn-signal lights legally replace hand signals, but low morning or evening sun on the lenses can make it hard to tell whether they are flashing. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec11-F33 | anchor: A04
Signal for at least the last 100 feet before turning or stopping, and at least the last 200 feet before a turn when the speed limit is 45 mph or higher. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec11-F34 | anchor: A04
Hand signals use the left arm out the driver's window: arm straight out with finger pointing for a left turn. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec11-F35 | anchor: A04
For a right turn by hand, hold the arm out with the forearm and hand raised and the palm forward. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec11-F36 | anchor: A04
To signal slowing or stopping by hand, point the arm and hand downward with the palm facing back. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec11-F37 | anchor: A04
If a driver follows too closely, change lanes and signal for that driver to pass; stay centered in your lane with space on both sides. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec11-F38 | anchor: A04
When facing two unavoidable dangers at once, give the most room to the one that is worst or most likely, such as a child on a bicycle rather than oncoming cars. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec11-F39 | anchor: A04
If two dangers are equally serious, such as oncoming traffic and parked cars, stop and let the oncoming vehicles pass before going on. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0071]

Misconceptions: pumping the pedal does not help anti-lock brakes, which need steady hard pressure; turn-signal lights are legal but not always visible in low sun; mirrors do not cover the rear corners, so a head check is still required; giving room to the riskier hazard can mean moving closer to oncoming cars; the horn is for reasonable warning only, not routine use; hand signals are harder to see at night than flashing signals.
Mnemonics: hand signals point the way, up is right, down is stop; look far ahead, glance back often, check over the shoulder; brake hard and hold with ABS.
Glossary: ABS means an anti-lock braking system that keeps wheels from locking under hard braking; blind spot means an area near the rear corners not visible in the mirrors; emergency flashers means all four turn signals blinking together as a warning; margin of safety means open space kept around your vehicle; carbon monoxide means a poisonous exhaust gas that can enter the cabin through a leak.
Dynamic facts: the fuel cost figures in this section are economic estimates that can drift with fuel prices and are flagged as dynamic.

corpus_stability.reason: The handbook prints a single revision date (Revised May 2025) on its back cover and states laws and fees are subject to change by the General Assembly; no sign of more than one revision per year in the selected pages.
